chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a slave who married without the permission of his master, so he said: 'That is up to his master; if he wishes, he validates it, and if he wishes, he separates them.'

I said: 'May God rectify you, indeed Al-Hakam ibn Uthaynah, and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and their companions, say that the foundation of the marriage is invalid, so the master's validation does not make it permissible for him.'
So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'He did not disobey God; he only disobeyed his master. So when he validates it, it is valid for him.'
And whenever the master is pleased with the contract, it is not for him to annul it thereafter.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave's marriage if contracted without the master's permission?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *ijaz* (ratification) in Fiqh, where a slave's marriage without prior consent is considered valid but subject to the master's discretion. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between disobedience to the master (*ma'siya lil-sayyid*) and disobedience to God, thereby refuting the view that the contract is void ab initio. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the rights of masters over slaves' marital unions, emphasizing that the master's subsequent approval cements the validity of the marriage.
